Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) / Pure Font Communications (2022). Mechanical Vapour Recompression (MVR) for Low Carbon Alumina Refining: MVR Technical and Commercial Feasibility Studies - A Summary Report. ARENA, Canberra, November 2022, 22 pp.

A communications summary by Pure Font Communications for ARENA of the two Alcoa Stage 1 reports: the MVR Evaporation Feasibility Study (alcoa_2022_001) and the MVR Retrofit and Commercialisation Report (alcoa_2022_002), both extracted. Every technology number it prints (65 tph evaporator KPI table: capital 77 vs 53 $M, gas 47 GJ/h, electricity 0.1 vs 3.3 MW, 22,819 t CO2e/yr; A$622M Wagerup retrofit with the full cost table; 611 tph steam, 2.88 Mtpa, 134 MW; $220 and $260 per annual tonne; A$4.5B and 1.2 GW Australia-wide) is reprinted from those reports, so nothing was extracted. Numbers not in the Alcoa reports, none technology-level: Australian alumina refining emitted 14.6 Mt CO2 in 2021 (Australian Aluminium Council data 2000-2021); digestion takes about two-thirds and calcination one-third of refinery thermal energy; about 85% of refinery energy input leaves as low-grade heat; ARENA funding A$11.3M (May 2021); Stage 2 is a full-scale 4 MW MVR module at Wagerup (later closed, see alcoa_2024_001).
